speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing intense itching and developing red bumps on your thigh and other parts of your body. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have noticed any new soaps, detergents, or insect bites recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies.

The history of intense itching, the presence of red bumps, and the recent travel to Miami (a potential hotspot) are highly suggestive. Given your history of diabetes, which can alter skin presentation, I need to confirm if anyone in your household or close contacts has developed similar symptoms recently. REQUEST TEST: Skin_scratch_test_for_sarcopteg_ova. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatoscopy_of_thigh_lesions.
